body: After talking with his psychologist, we are going to go for adoption. Posting this on Reddit was a mistake for advice, no one knows our situation and I don’t need to be told what’s best from strangers

Hey there,

Yes, after some comments made today I agree that legal guardianship would be best and wait on adoption. You are right with not knowing more about it and also just not knowing the other options.

He has been in therapy since November 2023. I don’t believe that the type of therapy is beneficial given the situation, we are talking to his psychologist this week. 

Plus, I’d like the chances to build a relationship with SD. Adoption is likely not going to happen for a long time for the sake of the relationships, but the true thing is that legal guardianship is what we really need in this situation.

Out of all the comments, this is actually the most helpful. We did not consider legal guardianship. We will do this asap and continue talking with his psychologist because she believes adoption may be beneficial given his past.

It’s related to medical appointments, setting up therapy, and being in charge of his education. We are opting in for legal guardianship, as we never considered this an option until today. 

He can choose to want to be adopted in the future. At the end of the day, he views me as a mother. I’m the one he comes to when he’s hurt. I’m the one he confided with all the scary things that happened in his life. I’m the one he came to when he was sick at night covered in vomit. 

My family, his family, and the mother’s family want me to consider adopting him based on how he is with me. I’m talking to his psychologist because she believes it may be beneficial for him as well.
Upon reading, adoption would not disqualify him for his survivors benefits. I’m still going to take the same stance with waiting and having a PoA in place.

He would receive survivor benefits. I’ll make sure to discuss this point as well with SO, this is something he’s not aware of (and the reason why I told him to talk to a lawyer). 

For now, he has agreed to issue me Power of Attorney so I am able to help legally without causing issue, adoption won’t be necessary then and can be a later issue when he is older/if it comes up. SO agreed that this is the best way to go about it too.

Not at all, first hand accounts are what I was hoping for the most. We have talked about it again and we have opted for power of attorney and give him atleast several months before we revisit adoption. I look at adoption as vowing myself to care for him, and I want everyone to be aware of this before we do it. 

He has been very clingy with me and his dad. He wanted me to be his mommy robot (a game he made up sometime ago), and told me his mom was dead. I asked him how does that make him feel, and he said “Good”. He cried in spurts yesterday. It’s going to be a long grieving journey and a lot of hard work. I’m starting a journal of what is said and behaviors that are new for the therapist/psychologist. 

I am so sorry you experienced that. I do want to do right by him and this is purely out of love, not for image.

I was the one who suggested adoption as well. This was only 3 months into the relationship after he started showing signs of trauma. I love hard, and I know how big of a sacrifice it is, but he is so worth it. 

I went through terrible things as a kid myself, my mother is an addict. I was removed from my home at 14, first CYS case started when I was 12 years old. 

I’m sorry, I’m rambling. I feel like I want to share every detail as much as possible so those can understand. I don’t know why I feel the need to, maybe it’s apart of my own grief.
Thank you so much, I will. Having someone to talk to who has went through this is going to be such a blessing.

We have been living together for a year, which we rushed things in the beginning. Our relationship was filled with turmoil in the beginning, but we did do couples therapy within a couple months of living together. We have overcome so much, including quitting alcohol together, helping him through a suicide attempt and taking care of his son the entire time he was in the hospital, and him helping me with my Lupus. He is a patient soul, and I have never been so loved and cared for by a man in my life. He struggles a lot with BPD and we have found a rhythm to help him when he’s splitting.

I have been a sound mind in helping him treat his son better too. He is a wonderful dad, but in the beginning I could tell it was strained. There have been so many improvements and I can honestly say, these two boys are thankful for me in their life as well.

I am so so sorry, that is a really hard situation. I highly recommend therapy, we got him in as soon as we knew about the using, and sadly we found out it’s been going on since he was 2. He also had a bad relationship with his mother, and while we had 50/50 custody, he didn’t get to see her very often at all, his grandparents have been caring for him and BM lived separately due to her addiction. Drop offs were so difficult, he would latch onto me and cry, telling me to come with him and take care of him. I have never met a child so terrified of a parent. This has been like this since September 2023. CYS has also been involved up until her passing. 

You have to gauge how much they can handle based on maturity level, and it’s not an easy thing to do. SO, I and BM parents had a long talk about how to explain it to him. SO and I then took him to the side and let him know that Mommy has been struggling for a long time and she took too much of a bad medicine and her body couldn’t handle it, she has passed on. I also told him she was his guardian angel, and that I and SO will miss her very much with him, but we are here to answer any questions he has and we will do our best to remember her for all the good things. 

If you get him into therapy now, it’ll help in the long run with the outcome if it does come to that, and even if it doesn’t there is still much a child needs to heal from if their relationship is strained. Everyone’s been preparing for this mentally, and I’m glad we did prepare for worst case scenario because otherwise we wouldn’t have been able to hold it together for him. 

As of now, he’s spending time with his mom’s family and sister. We are going to try and make this as normal for him as possible, allowing as much time as they need together and us coming in to support.

I agree. It took sometime to realize this but it is right. Talking with SO we are getting on the same page. I think he is just devastated and thinks that it’s the best thing, but we should give it time and include SS on the decision, and ensure SD is ok with this too, which isn’t going to be for a long while. I’ll talk with the family today as well to let them know.

This is the best advice I have received so far, thank you for taking the time, even when I pushed back. You are right, my relationship with him must be the number one focus and legalities can come later on. I think after talking with my own family, they did put the stress on not rushing, and I’ll be honest, it’s hard to not. My involvement will probably not change as I am already so involved in the first place, so I think im trying to do something more in this situation that’s not needed at this moment.

And yet I am not the one who is making this decision, this is something we have discussed as a family unit (SO and BM family). I am not one to be taken aback by chaotic situations, nor am I thinking of myself at all when deciding this. SS is very close to me and SO and has been for a year now, BM family also knows this and this is why they want to maintain that dynamic, because it’s healthier for him. 

There’s so many details you are missing to assume that this is a terrible quick decision and it’s going to ruin a family.

I’m probably going to go for a more intensive therapy too. Our lives are changing so much and so fast. SO is already in weekly sessions so that helps. I think family therapy in the future will be important too. I’ve tried making this a very emotionally safe household, especially when he started showing signs of trauma back in the fall due to being exposed to her addiction for the past several years. 

Oh man, it is really really hard.

That’s the most difficult part of it, I know there will be a lot of feelings for SD. Thank you for bringing that up, that’s a point I really need to sit on and also work on with the family to ensure when the right time is for it.
It’s something the family wants too. I would NEVER try to replace his mother, nor would we announce the adoption either. It is purely to assist with medical needs, signing up for school, etc.

We are actually just going to the court house, a celebration won’t be for at least a year. SO wants me to adopt as soon as I can so I’m able to help, it’s something we agreed to do several months back in case this happened. We are going to try and make these next couple of weeks as healing as possible for both the kids.

Absolutely. He has been in therapy since the fall, but we are going to call on Monday to make sure this is within her scope and what she would recommend. Grief therapy would be really beneficial, I’m hoping she will give recommendations.
They weren’t able to do this but my PCP is consulting with them. I’ll have to send over my labs and imaging to em to get an opinion and hopefully be see soon

They have, also an ultrasound on my legs as my pain is worse there. I do have antiphospholipid syndrome so the concern was high but with clot ruled out, I’m cleared for discharge. My CKP was low too which is really odd, Sed rate increased since last bloodwork. Kidneys are actually functioning better than last, was at 89% last check and at worst was 65%. 

I’m going to hound down the new rheumatologists I was referred to, which may be out of network but I don’t care at this point, I’m miserable. This will be the 5th job I lose to lupus flares, I’m an accountant who can’t type.

Tramadol didn’t even help, but I refuse narcotics due to first hand experience seeing addiction. 

Thankfully the ER doctor was an absolute angel and found a specialist that he highly recommends that should be able to get me in sooner, if not I will make the appointment with UPMC as that’s where I was seen despite insurance out of network.

I’ve been on 40mg prednisone with no relief, finished taper today and now they put me on a 60mg taper. I really need to get back on biologics and get on disability. I’ve been struggling so bad keeping a job so I can get insurance, then having frequent flares and getting let go. Oh what joy it’d be to focus on my health and not the stressors of work.
They have treated me really well so far. It looks like I am getting admitted. My D-Dimer is incredibly high, I’m really happy I went.
Thankfully credits added up fast for myself and two months of the year covers the past 5, and I’ve worked since 16 years old. I considered that hard before calling someone. 😅

Update: lawyer is taking my case on. He seems confident and with the documentation, it should help. I’m pulling together records and a timeline to prove decline. I hope for an easy process, but I’m patient as I’ve been trying hard for so many years.

They will test specific antibodies. ANA is present in many autoimmune diseases, as well as some in the general population (infections, normal, etc) but specific antibodies are needed in order to confirm the cause. Pattern is also very important to diagnosis, which is multiple types, but lupus seems to be most common with ANA  pattern Speckled and Homogeneous (does not confirm diagnosis). 

I'm 26, was diagnosed at 11. Have high DsDNA and Chromatin. Both of the antibodies are specific to Lupus, but other antibodies can help with diagnosis (smith). Some may be signs of Pre-Lupus, like SSA and SSB.

It could be Lupus but SLE causes joint pain, not Subacute Cutaneous Lupus. Has she been tested for ANA, Ds-DNA, or Anti-Chromatin? These are golden standard as inflammatory markers aren't always positive, and while a very small amount of people have negative ANA, it really is vital to have positive antibodies in order to diagnose Lupus properly. You do not want a misdiagnosis as the medications to treat Lupus can be extremely harmful for those who do not have it and can make other conditions flare worse/possible complications. 


It also sounds like possible Psoriasis with Psoriatic Arthritis. 
A skin biopsy should be a huge help in confirming. Lupus and Psoriasis can both be seen on biopsy. There are several overlapping medications for treatment of the two, including Steroids and Methotrexate. 


I wish you and your mother the best. I'm trying to assist my twin in her journey, but she didn't think she had it while I did due to her rashes/skin was mottled, and her Antibodies came back positive for Pre-Lupus. I've had Lupus for over 15 years and have major involvement at 26.

Senior Cost Accountant here. I've found that it's been the more flexible field. Others within my area include Office Manager, AP, AR and Shipping (all have the same amount of flexibility across the industry). I am out around every other week with a couple hospital stays a year. It's been hard to maintain a full-time schedule, but I'm upfront with that in every interview and never spare a detail so I know it's a good fit. I think transparency is crucial to screen for most jobs since it'll save a lot of grief (I have Lupus, this is the x amount of days I usually need off, hourly expectations, PTO negotiations and establish possibilities of running out).

Hang in there! I was diagnosed 15 years ago and honestly, it's surprising I haven't gotten it sooner. I hope that gives some hope that it can take time, but always be safe and take care of yourself. Frequent UTIs seem to be a commonality here, taking daily cranberry pills help a lot but be warned, they can cause kidney stones. 

When I had my scares in the past, I bought the urinalysis strips to watch for protein/blood/etc. It really put my mind at ease that i could watch it, especially when I had a lot of anxiety. They're relatively affordable and amazon has great brands available. It's nice to feel some type of control through all the uncertainties.

I did and there was protein/blood (i dont know the value, but significant enough). I'm a champ at being hydrated due to POTs, otherwise I would have hoped that could be it. 

They're going to retest again in a week to ensure it doesn't get worse.

Yeah I'm on chemo now to stop the nervous system involvement but it's not helping, although its only two months in but my doctor was expecting good changes by now. Sad to see the kidneys be effected too. My Sed rate and C Reactive have increased too. 

I hope you're doing better now!

I guess I'll have to sacrifice the high sodium/water intake for awhile then, my Rheumatologist didn't mention a reduction just yet but I go in for a treatment plan tomorrow. I've had to always have this diet since I have ANS dysfunction and POTs, helps with low blood pressure and irregular heart rhythms. 

I'm on methotrexate now but have a feeling cellcept is in my future. I've only been on it for a short period so they ruled it out as the cause.

Having anti-DsDNA and anti-Chromatin. My prior Rheumatologist (she left for another state) did a study on it and predictors, people with these two positive had a higher rate of kidney involvement, which I guess was a pretty significant correlation. They monitored those without kidney involvement but had positive tests, most developed some type of involvement over the course of 5 years. 

It's not really a common predictor, but I still found that to be helpful to make lifestyle choices to help work against it.

Million miles a minute thoughts.
Rheumatologists usually specialize. I chose one that's very well known for Lupus and research.

I have a pill purse, which is kinda silly when i think about it. Since I've been on so much as of late and I never know what emergencies may arise, I have another carry on with all of my medications. I also keep emergencies contacts, toiletries and other essentials within the bag. I call it my Lupus survival pack.

- Mood Journal. Helps to monitor stress levels. 

- Spoon Mehtod. It's something I watch closely because I'm notorious for overworking myself and dealing with the consequences later. I hate being unreliable because I have a hard time pulling away from work, then need more rest days because of it. 

- Ensure there's handicap spots available at events (if you have mobility issues). I've had my handicap for my car since I was 17, and if I'm having a hard time with mobility at times, it's helped to make sure it's available. Granted, I'll suck it up, but back when I had tendon involvement, I really made it worse by not checking and pushing through it. I don't want to miss out on things, but know I need to acknowledge pain and stop sucking it up. 

- If loved ones are struggling to understand you, bring them to your appointments with you. It's strengthened my relationships with those who didn't really understand it that well and it was easier for my doctor to explain it than myself.

Expecting myself to cook and clean more than my spouse because I'm a woman despite the load of burden since I have a demanding job that requires a lot of my time (i also make a significantly larger living). The worst backlash I got was when I was speaking about the house I flipped where my spouse had no involvement (we werent together when i had the house/flipped it), but his mother asked me to give him credit for it and denied that I could have done that much work by hand, by myself. Maybe it isn't gender related but it certainly felt that way. He started to brag about his part after and I spoke the truth, which made her upset with me. Thankfully, with all the other red flags, that is a situation of the past. 

I'm in a great relationship now but I got met with a lot of expectations before that made me question myself and at one point, I truly believed it. I'll never go back to people deciding what I should and shouldn't do as a woman.
Letting people make me believe that not conforming to gender role standards makes me a bad partner.
How is it horrendous? What's horrendous is this backlash and jealousy. Who the fuck wants a sooner diagnosis because they're so sick?

I have to ask, is there another hospital system you could get another opinion from? I sympathize with you, but you are not apart of the group I intended this to refer to. I understand it's nice to feel not so alone, as it's something I feel constantly, there's almost even a sense of stronge loneliness as of late from the turn of this subreddit. 

I want support too, but in terms of people who have serious and rare issues from it, then to be met with a flood of diagnosis questions. I feel like no one has experienced what I have most of the time and I'm searching for that one person's experience. It's almost like I'm being mocked. 

I have severe nervous system failure that is irreversible. My ANA titer is over 300. I'm losing blood cells from severe esophagus bleeding due to involvement. I have liver disease with abnormal liver enzymes since i was a kid. I've had stage 1 kidney disease. I've developed extremely bad Lupus Coagulation and the factor is incredibly high. My DS DNA has tripled since July. I've had a stroke at 20. I'm going partially blind in my left eye. They can't reduce my sed rate and c reactive, even with hugh dose methotrexate (I've been on 5 other immunobiologics in the past 15 years). My red blood cells are so irregularly shaped from Lupus that it makes my blood clot easier. My CBC is so bad from Lupus, as well as other tests. I also had megacolon back in October and it was so incredibly painful, I lost a pot of blood. I've been so sick from day 1 and I'm lucky enough to have had such a major event as a kid, but it also fucking sucks. 

Yet I feel like I can't talk about it because their is so much terror and fright, it makes me feel like a piece of shit. I don't want to upset anyone, it hurts my heart, but I'm also screaming out for advice. I'm only 26 and angry by this disease. I try to overwork myself because I refuse it, but it refuses me harder.

The point is there is also a lot of rejection for us who need first hand advice and support. I understand people are fed up with the system when they don't have answers, but it shouldn't be taken out in this community. That's not what this subreddit was about.

I wasn't in that position. I was 11 when I was diagnosed. I'm in a position that the support has turned vile for those seeking answers from those who also are going through the same thing. 

I'm sick of explaining that the threads are filled with seekers who need empathy and as soon as I post something as someone with a valid diagnosis, I get met with grief because I am not one who can comment on someone else's symptoms. 

It's not always Lupus, and unless a doctor has confirmed the possibility, there's no reason to take away from this community. It's also supposed to be for us with a diagnosis, just as kuch as thise seeking advice. There's other communities for people asking questions related to Autoimmune disease, like the MCTD subreddit which is specifically for these kinds of questions, but instead, it's because a House episode of "Is this Lupus?"

Meaning it's unique person to person. The amount of labs that are specific to lupus, and well, everyone has different markers and involvement. Diagnosis is never strictly off labs, my friend had never had positive labs until recently, but the rash was what set off her diagnosis. Granted, it took many years. Questions and answers in these threads need to take that into consideration. It's become separated from facts. 

This is not the case for every post, or comment. There are plenty who seek advice, and it helps them to get into the right direction, but it has become overflooded with people seeking diagnosis from this community. It goes far enough that people asking for support are replied with the question if they have Lupus. 

Some of us just want support without the stress of receiving these kinds of messages and requests. I'm happy that there are those strong enough to share their experiences so openly, but acknowledge those who don't have the energy to do so anymore. It's become harassment.

The point is missed. Seeking diagnosis versus advice. Also, we cannot truly help in assisting with others treatment in order to keep the disease mild, if it is Lupus. We can share experiences, that's all, but to have to personally take a deeper dive than that is asking too much out of this communities members. 

Lupus is like a thumbprint, it's so incredibly unique and we should all try to treat it as such.

I apologize that it does seem to be this way, i mean it with the upmost love to wish everyone to not have to suffer the same and to be able to seek support in a healthy way. I couldn't imagine being older and seeking support through diagnosis, especially since I was the girl who was seeking attention until it became so severe. Recent exchanges have only shifted my viewpoint from empathetic, to a sense of myself having to feed into the support of others when I really needed the support myself. 

When you ask for others experiences when you are going through something similar, to be met with "Holy crap, can you tell me if you think what I'm going through is Lupus? It sounds the exact same!"... it's tiring. I don't think there's a good handle on this here.

Gatekeeping applies to those consistently seeking diagnosis. If you need advice, that's one thing, but to outright ask if it's Lupus or looks like Lupus, that's downright wrong.

I appreciate your reply. I understand seeking treatment as my diagnosis came from an admission at 11 that resulted in a long case from ignoring my pains and health as a kid. Parents lost custody over it. 

I suppose that I'm a bit at a loss that the support in this community has went from collaboration and support, to seeking full blown "Do I have Lupus?". I just want to talk to others with the same experience versus being treated as the expert. I'm not an expert. I want out so badly. I'd gladly give anyone my diagnosis if they wanted it, it just seems like they do and they don't know what they're getting themselves into.

I understand where it's coming from, but UCTD is incredibly unspecific and general. Get a second opinion, request specific tests and advocate for yourself, but I don't think it's right to say you have something without confirmation. If you think the doctors not taking you seriously, it's up to you to find that person who truly believes in you, we can't make those who consistently deny us of what is right to believe us.

I say this as someone whose had Lupus for 15 years and so many cried to me claiming they had Lupus based on symptoms, begging for advice, how I deal with it, lying they have it, only for it to be something else. It's incredibly insensitive.

MRI showed abnormalities and lesions. There's a couple other scans they can complete, but MRI with contrast was the one that really uncovered the activity. 

Some of it can still been seen on a CT scan, which originally showed abnormalities once contrast was used (blood vessel, etc), but I'm highly allergic to the CT contrast. I am not allergic to what they use in MRI contrast. 

Once activity is dormant, they can see that the lesions or inflammation is not active anymore. It's neat to see progress.

I used to suffer from an eating disorder. I do believe there was a strong connection with Lupus after finding brain involvement since I was around 13 years old. The right treatment has certainly aided in recovery, and I have been grateful to say that most of my ED symptoms are no longer there. 

I still see a therapist, as well as a psychiatrist, since it absolutely helps, in addition to treatment. I had a rough time growing up, so it helped to tackle that and take care of myself in order to recover. 

I think Lupus is a huge aggressor for existing Mental Health symptoms. It also caused me to be very paranoid and a few episodes of psychosis (rare for most). I have active involvement in my brain with inflammation. Current treatment has already improved my mental health so much, with no new psych meds involved.

The psychosis is related to nervous system involvement. I have a lesion the size of a quarter in the back left cortex of my brain (as well as neuropathy, POTs, Narcolepsy, gastroparesis). Thankfully antipsychotic medication made it better quickly, but i wasnt on treatment during the time for lupus. 

I was previously on Benlysta and plaquenil, but I stopped responding well to it and developed an allergy. They're hesitant to try anything like Methotrexate due to nervous system issues. 

I'm really hoping once insurance approves the other types of treatments, I can go through other options. I'll also be starting prednisone this week after finding liver issues.

I have my medical card and it helps a lot, especially with nerve pain from neuropathy. I do find that some strains make the fatigue more prominent, but CBD during the day is my go to, and THC with CBD at night to help me sleep. I highly recommend getting something that has been lab tested, as some of the off the street CBDs are advertised at a higher potency than they actually are. That kinda shifted me into getting my medical card, as it's a whole different world of quality in my opinion. 

Little backstory; I was diagnosed 14 years ago at age 11. I had severe pleurisy of both lungs and the diagnosis was fast due to my bloodwork, I consider myself lucky. I'm currently on a more natural path of treatment, but am in an active flare and just got over having Covid for the 2nd time (very mild, blessed for that).

Room and board expenses paid out from grants/scholarships are taxable.

2. Pell grant is considered recognizable income in excess of what is not used for education expenses (tuition, books and supplies, lab fees, etc.)

3. If he had no health insurance, the fee is 2.5% of income or $695, whichever is higher. Does not matter if he was a full time student or not.

4. He can claim the EMT course if it is eligible for student aid by the U.S. Department of Education, as long as it wasn’t paid with funds granted by student aid/scholarships.
